overview: This bill would create the Ralph David Abernathy, Sr., National Historic Site in Atlanta, Georgia, as part of the National Park System. It would preserve the historic West Hunter Street Baptist Church, where Dr. Abernathy served as pastor during the height of the civil rights movement, and tell the story of his role as a civil rights leader. The site would be officially established only once the Interior Department, which runs the National Park Service, has acquired enough land to manage it. Land could be gained by donation, purchase from willing sellers, or exchange, and state or local government land only by donation. The Park Service would write a management plan within 3 years of receiving funding and could partner with the state and others on signs, exhibits and tours. As of July 23, 2026, the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee had approved it and it was waiting for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say the site would preserve an important civil rights landmark and make sure Dr. Abernathy's role in the movement is remembered and taught.
against: Critics say adding a new national park unit adds to the Park Service's costs and maintenance needs at a time when it already has a large backlog of repairs.
